blocks.text: Have you ever wondered why the government sometimes sets the price of essential goods like petrol or rice?

blocks.markdown: Price control is a regulatory measure by the government to set the prices of goods and services in the market. This is often done to protect consumers and ensure that essential goods remain affordable.

blocks.title: Price Ceiling
blocks.text: A price ceiling is the maximum price set by the government for a particular good or service, below the equilibrium price, to make it affordable for consumers.

blocks.markdown: In Nigeria, the government sometimes imposes price ceilings on essential goods like petrol to prevent them from becoming too expensive for the average consumer. This is crucial in maintaining affordability and preventing inflation.

blocks.title: Price Floor
blocks.text: A price floor is the minimum price set by the government for a particular good or service, above the equilibrium price, to ensure producers receive a fair price.

blocks.title: Understanding Price Ceilings
blocks.prompt: Consider a market where the equilibrium price of rice is ₦500 per bag. The government sets a price ceiling at ₦400. What happens in this market?

steps.text: Identify the equilibrium price and the price ceiling.
Since the price ceiling is below the equilibrium price, a shortage occurs as demand exceeds supply.

blocks.answer: A price ceiling below the equilibrium price leads to a shortage.

blocks.markdown: Price controls can lead to unintended consequences. For instance, a maximum price below equilibrium can cause shortages, as seen in the petrol market in Nigeria.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Remember, a price ceiling is set below the equilibrium price, while a price floor is set above it.

points: Price ceilings are used to keep essential goods affordable.
Price floors ensure producers receive a fair price for their goods.
